value_leaf_table.derivation: PLAY SCALARS use only in-play depths (<= h_conv_depth_cap): h_conv = min heuristic_lp over those; value_trust_depth = min{d<=cap: value_leaf_lp[d]-h_conv <= tol}; value_no_fallback likewise. (Deep cells d>cap extend the table+crossover for the anchor but do NOT move the escalation gate; a trust_depth > search_depth is equivalent to UNSET in play.) crossover spans ALL depths.

value_fallback_crossover.rule: after escalating a value-leaf line committed at depth c, TAKE the heuristic line iff hcommitted >= take_heuristic_at_hdepth[c] (else keep the leaf). Clamp c/hcommitted to the measured [min,max] depth. Per-committed-depth (NOT a uniform offset).

value_play.note: MEASURED 2026-08-04 (100k games/arm, 20 paired seeds, trust=5 both arms): d5 is 6.3% FASTER than d6 but WORSE on the metric, +0.00059 turns, paired t=+6.17, 18/20 seeds worse, 95% CI [+0.00040,+0.00078]. d6 is kept for QUALITY. NOTE the previous rationale here ('d6 ~10-20% faster than d5-escalate at identical quality') is VOID: it was measured at value_trust_depth=6, where escalate_below=6 forced an escalation on every depth-<=5 commit, so the d5 arm was crippled by construction. At trust=5 a depth-5 commit is trusted and the escalation counts match (330 vs 331), which is why d5 now measures faster. Re-derive this if trust moves again.

provenance.note: eval_model retrained on rows dumped at SHIPPED play WITH the deck profile, so the exhaustive keep model was live. Labels are searched K=3 for every deck (a pooled dump forces one label mode). value_leaf_table/crossover here are the OLD ones until the regenerated matrix lands.
